assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made a superconducting artificial atom strongly coupled to a single microwave photon in a resonator, giving dispersive readout, coupling buses and the architecture used by essentially all superconducting processors. Originality, clarity and breadth of impact are exceptional; it is the common platform for circuit and waveguide QED, and a decisive step from macroscopic quantum circuits to controllable quantum machines.
assessment.attribution: The theory proposal (Blais and collaborators, with Girvin and Huang among the proposers in the literature I recall) and the first strong-coupling experiment (Wallraff, Schoelkopf and colleagues) are naturally paired. The supplied three names form a coherent theory-plus-experiment configuration. Others, such as Girvin, are not in the supplied credit and cannot be proposed.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of independent confirmation in many laboratories, with cQED underlying mature technology. Timing is not premature, though the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits sits close to this field.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wants to recognise superconducting circuits again so soon after 2025.
The credit list omits proposers I recall (e.g. Girvin), so the fairness of a three-person split is not fully settled.
As a circuit-QED theorist I may be partial to this field; I have not independently verified priority details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum error correction (Shor's nine-qubit code, Steane's CSS codes, Kitaev's toric code and anyonic fault tolerance) showed that quantum information can be protected against noise, so scalable quantum computing is possible in principle. This is among the deepest conceptual results in quantum information and sets the central engineering goal of every hardware programme, including the superconducting one I work on.
assessment.attribution: Shor and Steane independently produced the first codes and Kitaev the topological codes and fault-tolerance framework. Calderbank, Gottesman and others also made decisive contributions that the supplied credit does not allow me to propose, so any three-person split is somewhat arbitrary.
assessment.maturity: Theory is decades old and validated by logical-qubit demonstrations, including recent below-threshold surface-code experiments, though these are still small and a full fault-tolerant machine does not yet exist. Recognition is arguably timely and arguably early on the experimental side.
uncertainties: Attribution is genuinely contested among several originators not on the list.
Experimental maturity of fault tolerance is still evolving.
Part of this work is mathematics or computer science, which could raise a disciplinary-fit question for physics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for ion-trap quantum gates, and their broader theory of quantum simulation and quantum optics with trapped atoms and ions, provided the first concrete architecture for a quantum computer and a template for atomic quantum simulation. Originality and impact are very high and the work links directly to all platforms discussed in quantum computing.
assessment.attribution: The pair is a clean two-person credit with well-recognised joint authorship of the 1995 proposal. Experimental realisation is the work of others (e.g. Wineland and Blatt groups) that this candidate does not cover, and Wineland was recognised in 2012.
assessment.maturity: The proposal has been confirmed in many ion-trap experiments over thirty years and now underlies commercial devices. Recognition is mature and not premature.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize for controlling individual quantum systems may reduce novelty for the committee.
This candidate overlaps with the optical-lattice and Rydberg candidates, so the committee must avoid double counting.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Bistritzer-MacDonald flat-band theory and the observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states at the magic angle opened the large field of moire quantum matter. The theory predicted the magic angle and the experiments realised a tunable strongly correlated platform. Originality and impact are very high and the field has expanded to many 2D materials.
assessment.attribution: A theory-plus-experiment pairing is natural, with Jarillo-Herrero leading the experiments and MacDonald and Bistritzer the continuum-model theory. The first experimental authors of the 2018 papers are not in the supplied credit, and the allocation between Bistritzer and MacDonald is a judgement call. Three names is the maximum, so I propose all three.
assessment.maturity: Experiments have been reproduced by many groups for years and the interpretation of the correlated phases is still being refined. The superconducting mechanism remains debated, but the discovery itself is robust.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism for the superconductivity is unresolved.
Experimental credit beyond Jarillo-Herrero is not in the supplied list.
Possibly early for a field that is still rapidly developing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson at the LHC in 2012 confirmed the mechanism for electroweak symmetry breaking predicted decades earlier and completed the Standard Model's particle content. The importance and clarity of the result are beyond doubt, and it followed the 2013 prize to the theorists.
assessment.attribution: Credit is difficult. Two collaborations of thousands of people each, and four named leaders (Gianotti, Della Negra, Jenni, Virdee) who are all credited but only three may be selected. My choice of Gianotti, Jenni and Virdee leaves out Della Negra and is a judgement about leadership roles, not a verified assessment of decisive contribution. The prize rules also make a collaboration award difficult.
assessment.maturity: Discovery confirmed independently by ATLAS and CMS and by later Tevatron and precision measurements, and the couplings are increasingly well measured. Recognition is mature.
uncertainties: The prize-rule problem of recognising large collaborations and the choice of individuals.
Selecting three of four credited names is unavoidably contested.
Whether the 2013 prize already makes a second award for the same discovery less likely.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BB84 and E91 established quantum key distribution and the idea that quantum entanglement and measurement can secure communication, giving a foundational application of quantum foundations. Impact is large across quantum information science and quantum communication technology, and conceptual clarity is high.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard share the clear priority for BB84 (with Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea outside this list) and Ekert authored the entanglement-based protocol E91. This is a natural three-person configuration within the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Experimental demonstrations, satellite links and commercial systems are well established. The 2022 prize for entanglement tests partly overlaps, but QKD is a distinct discovery.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 prize on Bell tests and quantum information science.
The practical security of implemented systems differs from the idealised protocol.
Priority questions around earlier conjugate-coding work by Wiesner.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 topological insulator (Kane and Mele), with the HgTe experimental observation of edge transport (Molenkamp), launched topological band theory as a central theme of condensed-matter physics. The impact on materials physics and on quantum-computing ideas (Majorana platforms) is substantial.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the theoretical prediction and Molenkamp's group the first experimental realisation of the 2D state. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang predicted the HgTe realisation and Hasan, who is credited here, led the three-dimensional work. The supplied list has four names so I have to leave one out, which is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed across many materials and a mature field, though the 2016 prize on topological phase transitions already covers part of the conceptual background.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2016 prize and with the quantum anomalous Hall candidate.
Exclusion of Hasan and of uncredited theorists such as Zhang and Bernevig is contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks use the magic-wavelength idea of Katori and the strontium clock developments of Ye to reach fractional uncertainties near 1e-18, redefining the limits of precision measurement and enabling tests of fundamental physics and relativistic geodesy. The concept is original and clear and the impact on metrology is large.
assessment.attribution: The credit is a clean pair, with Katori for the magic-wavelength lattice concept and Ye for the high-accuracy realisations and comparisons. Other groups have important contributions (for example Lemke and Ludlow at NIST), so allocation is not totally unproblematic.
assessment.maturity: Independent clocks around the world have confirmed the performance and a redefinition of the second is under discussion, so the result is well established. The 2005 comb prize is a related but distinct honour.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2005 and 1997 laser-cooling and spectroscopy prizes in the committee's thinking.
The ongoing redefinition of the second suggests the technology is still maturing.
